mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the subsequent month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30-day period of lower rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% while UNRATE falls by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns fail to outperform a 30-day baseline during similar labor market conditions (rolling IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% suggests accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future earnings and supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL growth exceeding 0.3% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month indicates supply-side weakness, which raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly worse than during a prior non-shock period (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS turns positive after a sustained negative trend, it indicates a shift toward rate easing, which lowers real discount rates and supports positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS turns positive after <3 consecutive months of negative values
failure_condition: 5-day returns are flat or negative despite the easing signal (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding increase in layoffs suggests a tight labor market, which can fuel wage growth and equity risk appetite, yielding positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months without a decline
failure_condition: 60-day returns underperform a 30-day baseline during similar labor market conditions (rolling IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (not available in evidence, so skip) would be ideal but since confidence is missing, instead use a decline in RSAFS (retail sales) by >4% as a proxy for weak demand-supply balance, predicting negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% and RSAFS falls by >4% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative relative to a baseline of balanced supply conditions (rolling IC > -0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% month-over-month for two months), persistent increases in FEDFUNDS rates above 4% are expected to dampen equity valuations, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% MoM for 2 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 4% for the following month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL remains elevated (rolling IC > -0.05).
